tasks.short: Prepare for hearings, argue motions, question witnesses, and handle procedural exchanges with the court.

steps.what: Read pleadings, witness accounts, and procedural orders to prepare a hearing brief.

loop.input: Approved case documents and a fixed hearing-brief template.
loop.output: Draft hearing brief with document and page references.
loop.check: Validate references mechanically; lawyer checks disputed facts, omissions, and confidentiality.
loop.stop: One draft and two correction attempts; unresolved passages return to the lawyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Witness accounts and pleadings express material facts in varied free text.

steps.what: Choose motion arguments, witness questions, and responses to likely procedural challenges.
Confirm attendance, hearing arrangements, and access to the document bundle.
Argue motions, question witnesses, address the court, and select jurors where applicable.
Record court directions and assign follow-up actions after the hearing.

loop.input: Lawyer's hearing note and available written court directions.
loop.output: Proposed actions, owners, and dates linked to their source passages.
loop.check: Lawyer resolves discrepancies and approves deadline entries before internal publication.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; ambiguous directions remain unassigned for manual resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Oral directions recorded in narrative notes do not have reliable fixed fields.

tasks.design: A hearing-pack generator uses templates in the {DOCS} and a bounded extraction loop to prepare source-linked briefs. Configured flows in the {WORKFLOW} coordinate attendance through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, then publish approved follow-up actions to the {PROJECT}. The lawyer chooses tactics and conducts the hearing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case documents vary widely, while hearing strategy depends on context and changing courtroom dynamics.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document access, templates, and scheduling rules cover much of the support work. AI-assisted coding makes the connecting software cheaper to build; bounded extraction handles narrative documents.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, privilege, procedural surprises, and tactical concessions remain difficult. National rules determine rights of audience and whether juror selection exists.
tasks.human_edge: The lawyer reads the room, challenges testimony fairly, and makes accountable decisions under pressure.

ambition.what: A pre-hearing rehearsal for a first-time witness.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling papers and recording actions, leaving more time for witness preparation. Authority to conduct proceedings does not change.

reach.task: Prepare the hearing bundle and verify exhibit references.
reach.learn: Court bundle conventions, document provenance, and version control.

evidence.claim: Document review and drafting capabilities are available today; this does not establish courtroom automation.
Citation and case-law checks remain the lawyer's responsibility under Dutch professional guidance.
Attendance workflows and structured action tracking can use deterministic software.

assumptions: The setting is a specialist litigation team within a mid-size legal-services employer.
Civil hearings are the baseline; criminal proceedings and juror selection apply only where the practice and national rules permit.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Live representation dominates time, so preparation gains do not automate most of this task.
The build covers one practice area and existing systems. Access estimates include confidentiality review, GDPR arrangements, and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Jurisdictions, hearing types, and the lawyer's rights of audience.
Existing document templates, integrations, and confidentiality restrictions.
Whether employee-output monitoring is planned and consultation is required.
research_questions: Which national procedural rules govern witness preparation, hearing bundles, and courtroom technology?
Which existing interfaces support restricted document retrieval and calendar updates?
new_work: Check brief references and omitted adverse facts.
Resolve ambiguous court directions before recording deadlines.
Maintain hearing templates, access permissions, and notification rules.

tasks.short: Organise evidence, decide how to use it, and present it in litigation.

steps.what: Collect evidence files and maintain an exhibit index.
Assess relevance, authenticity, admissibility, and weaknesses in the proposed evidence.
Draft the evidence narrative and link each factual proposition to exhibits.

loop.input: Lawyer's outline, evidence assessment, and approved exhibits.
loop.output: Draft narrative with proposition-to-exhibit links and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Resolve every exhibit reference; lawyer checks factual support, adverse evidence, and permitted use.
loop.stop: One draft and two corrections; unsupported propositions remain flagged for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Connecting varied testimony and documents into a coherent narrative requires free-text drafting.

steps.what: Present evidence, answer challenges, and adapt submissions to the court's rulings.
Update exhibit status and record evidentiary rulings.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator indexes, versions, and paginates evidence held in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop turns the lawyer's outline into a source-linked presentation, while a configured register in the {WORKFLOW} records exhibit status. The lawyer decides admissibility positions and presents the evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence bundles mix formats and versions, and factual narratives require substantial reading. Ordinary indexing software does not decide what evidence proves.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic indexing and reference checks can be connected quickly. Bounded drafting can use a closed evidence set and expose unsupported propositions.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity, missing context, contradictory testimony, and admissibility need legal judgement. A valid document link does not establish that a proposition is true.
tasks.human_edge: The lawyer tests the evidence, explains uncertainty, and responds to objections without overstating the record.

ambition.what: An early adverse-evidence briefing before settlement discussions.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less bundle assembly and more scrutiny of weak evidence. The lawyer retains existing rights to choose and present the case.

reach.task: Maintain exhibit provenance and identify gaps in the evidence bundle.
reach.learn: Authentication requirements, evidentiary status, and reliable document comparison.

evidence.claim: Tabular document review and drafting are available capabilities.
A legal-research benchmark found material error rates, supporting substantive checks beyond valid references.
Exhibit numbering, duplicate detection, and pagination can use deterministic code.

assumptions: The setting is a litigation team within a mid-size legal-services employer.
Civil litigation is the baseline; criminal defence requires suitable expertise and authority. Public prosecution is not assumed.
Evidence is lawfully available to the team and originals remain preserved.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates; evidence preparation offers more scope than live presentation.

Build estimates cover a limited set of document formats and one document repository. Access work includes GDPR processor arrangements where applicable and consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Evidence formats, volumes, languages, and source-access restrictions.
Existing exhibit numbering and chain-of-custody practices.
Whether the court accepts electronic presentation and in which formats.
research_questions: Which national rules govern electronic evidence, redaction, and exhibit authentication?
Which extraction methods preserve the required provenance for the relevant file formats?
new_work: Review unsupported propositions and missing adverse evidence.
Resolve duplicate files, poor scans, and conflicting exhibit versions.
Maintain numbering conventions, access controls, and export formats.

tasks.short: Administer probate matters and advise executors on estate obligations and decisions.

steps.what: Meet the executor to establish instructions, family circumstances, and urgent estate issues.
Request missing records and track responses from the executor and institutions.
Compile assets, debts, beneficiaries, and supporting references into an estate inventory.

loop.input: Estate records, will, and a fixed inventory schema.
loop.output: Draft inventory with source references, dates, and unresolved ownership flags.
loop.check: Validate totals and duplicates deterministically; paralegal checks amounts, identities, and source dates.
loop.stop: Two extraction attempts per document; unreadable or conflicting records enter the exception list.
loop.why_not_simpler: Institutional statements and testamentary documents contain relevant information in varied layouts and prose.

steps.what: Determine authority, entitlement, liabilities, and whether specialist or cross-border advice is needed.
Prepare required probate applications and supporting schedules from approved estate information.
Advise the executor on obligations and obtain required declarations and filing approval.
Submit the authorised application and retain the filing receipt.

tasks.design: A configured estate register in the {WORKFLOW} tracks requested records and reminders through the {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop creates a source-linked inventory from the {DOCS}; deterministic calculations and templates generate probate forms and schedules. The lawyer advises the executor and authorises filing through the {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records arrive piecemeal from institutions and relatives. Forms are repeatable, but ownership, entitlement, and family disputes resist simple rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and form generation need established technology. Bounded extraction reduces rekeying, and AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting the register, documents, and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Contested wills, uncertain ownership, cross-border estates, tax questions, and vulnerable beneficiaries require specialists. National rules determine which legal professionals may conduct probate work.
tasks.human_edge: The lawyer explains duties sensitively, recognises conflicts, and challenges a proposed distribution when the legal position is uncertain.

ambition.what: An executor readiness review before the probate application is prepared.

tasks.altitude: The lawyer spends less time chasing records and correcting schedules, and more time advising on difficult estate decisions. Distribution and filing authority remain governed by the mandate and national rules.

reach.task: Reconcile estate inventory entries to institutional records.
reach.learn: Valuation dates, ownership evidence, duplicate detection, and escalation of disputed entries.

evidence.claim: Template-driven legal document production has documented productivity gains, but the cited trial did not establish probate outcomes.
Document-set review capabilities exist; probate inventory accuracy requires separate validation.
GDPR processor-contract requirements apply where a processor handles personal data for the practice.
Estate totals, completeness checks, and form population can use deterministic software.

assumptions: This is a specialist private-client team within a mid-size legal-services employer; probate is uncommon in an ordinary corporate legal department.
The baseline is an uncontested estate in one jurisdiction with an authorised executor or administrator.
A relevant filing route through the {GOV_PORTAL} exists; paper or professional filing routes require adaptation.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates. Document work is more reducible than legal advice.

Build estimates cover one jurisdiction and a small form set. Access work includes estate mandates, GDPR arrangements for living persons' data, and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Applicable jurisdiction, professional authority, and estate complexity.
Required executor approvals, declarations, and signature methods.
Available record formats, institutional access, and filing routes.
research_questions: Which national rules govern probate authority, beneficiary protection, and required declarations?
Which official forms, valuation conventions, and filing requirements apply?
new_work: Verify extracted amounts, ownership, beneficiaries, and valuation dates.
Handle missing records and contradictory institutional responses.
Maintain form versions, calculation rules, and approved reminder templates.
Check approval evidence and filing receipts.

tasks.short: Research and draft legal briefs and opinions, then prepare and file authorised appeals.

steps.what: Assess appeal grounds, procedural route, deadlines, and the client's objectives.
Assemble the relevant record, judgment, and document references.
Research legislation and case law using licensed legal research sources.

loop.input: Legal questions and licensed, jurisdiction-filtered legislation and case-law sources.
loop.output: Research note with linked authorities, relevant passages, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Resolve citations in the source base; lawyer checks currency, jurisdiction, holdings, and adverse authorities.
loop.stop: Two failed retrieval or citation repairs return the question to manual research.
loop.why_not_simpler: Legal questions and judgments require semantic reading; keyword retrieval alone cannot produce the analysis.

steps.what: Draft the brief or opinion using the record, authorities, and argument outline.

loop.input: Approved outline, verified research, indexed record, and jurisdiction-specific template.
loop.output: Draft brief with record references and citations; missing support remains marked.
loop.check: Check required sections and references automatically; lawyer verifies reasoning, quotations, and factual support.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted corrections; remaining gaps go to the lawyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover structure and fixed text, but case-specific legal reasoning needs free-text drafting.

steps.what: Review the complete document and authorise its release or filing.
Submit the approved appeal and required attachments through the court filing route.
Save the filing receipt and update matter status and deadline reminders.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles the appeal record from the {DOCS}, while a bounded research loop reads licensed legal sources through the {OTHER}. Templates generate fixed sections, and a bounded drafting loop prepares case-specific reasoning for lawyer review. Following authorised manual filing through the {GOV_PORTAL}, configured flows update the {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR} from confirmed receipt details and verified dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research sources, case records, and drafting templates are disconnected. Free-text legal reasoning and unreliable citations prevent unattended generation.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked research and drafting capabilities already exist. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of record assembly, reference validation, template generation, and status updates.
tasks.still_hard: An appeal may turn on a narrow procedural issue, adverse authority, or an incomplete record. Valid citations can still misstate the law, and filing routes differ under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The lawyer chooses defensible grounds, states adverse law honestly, and accepts responsibility for the final submission.

ambition.what: A fixed-scope appeal viability opinion for clients facing a short decision window.

tasks.altitude: The lawyer spends less time assembling records and writing initial text, and more time testing arguments. Filing authority and responsibility for the opinion remain unchanged.

reach.task: Validate record references and prepare the filing package.
reach.learn: Appellate record limits, citation verification, filing rules, and receipt reconciliation.

evidence.claim: A firm trial reported 45% time savings on first-draft legal briefings; this is not an estimate for the entire appeal task.
Legal research, drafting, and review capabilities are available for specified European legal sources.
A legal-research benchmark documented substantial errors, supporting manual checks of legal propositions.
Dutch professional guidance requires lawyers to check citations and remain responsible.

assumptions: The setting is a litigation team within a mid-size legal-services employer.
National appeal structures replace the original task's US court terminology.
The steps show an appeal matter; a standalone opinion ends after authorised release and excludes filing steps.
Licensed source access permits the proposed retrieval and processing.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates, not transfers of trial results.
Build estimates cover one jurisdiction, source collection, and filing-package format. Access work includes GDPR arrangements and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
Status automation uses confirmed receipt fields and existing verified dates; it does not infer new legal deadlines from narrative orders.
unknowns: Applicable jurisdictions, appeal types, and mandatory representation rules.
Source licences, retrieval interfaces, and document-access permissions.
Approval mandates, filing routes, and receipt formats.
Existing deadline validation and escalation practices.
research_questions: Which national rules determine appeal deadlines, permitted grounds, signatures, and service requirements?
Which licensed sources support version-aware retrieval and persistent citation links?
Which court interfaces support reliable receipt capture?
new_work: Check cited holdings, quotations, source currency, and adverse authorities.
Review reasoning and record references before authorising release.
Maintain templates, source connectors, and procedural rules.
Resolve filing failures and unmatched receipts.

role.altitude: The lawyer's week shifts from document assembly and initial drafting towards evidence testing, client advice, and advocacy. Preparation improves, while legal decision rights remain tied to professional authority and client instructions.
reach: Paralegals: evidence provenance, record completeness, and citation validation.
Legal assistants: controlled intake, filing preparation, and deadline administration.
skills_to_grow: Separate fixed procedural rules from case-specific legal judgement.
Verify source support rather than merely checking that citations exist.
Design document templates, exception queues, and approval points.
Understand confidential-data access, GDPR duties, and applicable national professional rules.
Evaluate extraction and drafting on representative matters before wider rollout.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a fixed-scope early case assessment combining a verified evidence map, a source-linked legal analysis, and a lawyer-led discussion of options.
